about.published: false while there are no records under records/pools: the first board series is not published yet
about.boards: per board directory of records/pools (records_dir): id (the board's id on the site's other kinds), the record's board, board_decoded, core and clock_hz; note_cache_off: the sentence the CRC results page puts above the board's cache-off numbers (site/crc_tables.py, before_off), or null
about.scenarios: the scenarios of kinds/pools/README.md ("The image"), with what is timed, in one line each; 'init' is one call
about.configurations: per adapter, in the order of kinds/pools/configs.txt: its name (the record's), language (column 2), and from the table "The set" of kinds/pools/README.md its library, pin, licence and the lock as built; role: 'library', or 'ours' for our reference free list with interrupts off (not a library, labelled in its name cell every time; scored like any row; a filter on the kind of row leaves it out); documented_interrupts: what the library documents about use from interrupts, with its source (kinds/pools/claims.tsv): shown as documented (the timing series is one context; whether it holds is tested by the concurrency series, each row's 'isr'), and used in no score
about.baseline_documented: the claims file's row of the baseline (adapter_ref), shown in the baseline's row
about.rows: per board and configuration: flash_bytes (the record's sizes.flash_bytes: code and constant data) and ram_bytes (the record's sizes.ram_overhead_bytes: RAM beyond the 1056 bytes of blocks and canaries; kinds/pools/README.md, "Sizes"), the record's path, and cycles
about.cycles: cycles[cache][key]: [min, max] over the eight placements, first pass, of the mean of the scenario's calls (the first call included), in cycles, the counter-read overhead subtracted; key 'init' (one call) or '<scenario>/<alloc|free>'; null where the scenario has no such call (empty/free)
about.baseline: per board: the reference free list (ours, not a library), timed in the same images (the records' baseline), cycles over all images of the board's library configurations
about.ranges: a difference between two rows is a difference only where their ranges do not overlap (DECISIONS 2026-11-25); the rows are in the order of kinds/pools/configs.txt, not ranked
about.not_here: the second pass and the minimum, maximum and first call of each scenario: in the records
about.isr: per row: the concurrency series (records/pools-isr, lab/plans/2026-11-27-pools-concurrency.md): class ('within' its documentation, 'ours', 'outside' its documentation, 'control'); result: for 'within' and 'ours' passed or what was observed, for 'outside' only what was observed (never a verdict: the library was used in a way it does not document), for a control caught or not; trials; observed (kinds); irq_wait_cycles {off, on}, where the configuration takes interrupts off as built: the longest time an interrupt waited; coverage [instructions reached, instructions]; record. Used in no score; the comparison page offers a filter on it. null where the series has no record of the row
about.isr_variants: per row, where the series has one: another build of the same library, a configuration of its own in the concurrency series and not the build the row's numbers come from (C_Allocator with its lock option ALLOC_LOCK_CMSIS_RTOS2): adapter, name, documented_interrupts (kinds/pools/claims.tsv), and its result in the form of 'isr'
about.baseline_isr: per board: the reference free list without a lock, which the concurrency series runs as a control (it must be caught), in the form of 'isr'
about.isr_controls: per board: our two broken interrupts-off builds of the reference, the series' other controls

scenarios.text: one call that creates the pool in the adapter's storage
alloc, then free of the same block, 256 times, the pool almost empty
the same with 31 of the 32 blocks held
8 times: 32 allocs, then 32 frees in reverse order
8 times: 32 allocs, then 32 frees in the order of the allocs
512 calls from a fixed seed, the pool between 25 % and 75 % full
256 allocs on an exhausted pool, each of which must fail; no free

boards.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 H
boards.board_decoded: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 H (RP2350A, core 0, Cortex-M33)

boards.name: NUCLEO-H723ZG
boards.note_cache_off: The NUCLEO-H723ZG runs at 520 MHz with 3 flash wait states (voltage scale 0), as ST's template for the board sets it (`firmware/common/stm32h723/board.h`, method version 3). RM0468 (Table 16) requires 3 wait states for its AXI clock of 260 MHz. The numbers with the cache off carry the 3 wait states.

configurations.name: ThreadX block pool (C)
configurations.lock: interrupts off (TX_DISABLE), the release's port for each core

documented_interrupts.text: allocate and release allowed from ISRs; allocate from an ISR only with TX_NO_WAIT

configurations.name: CMSIS-RTX osRtxMemoryPool (C)
configurations.pin: v5.9.1, b566de4 (with CMSIS 6 af1b110, Cortex_DFP cd38dbb)
configurations.lock: LDREX/STREX on Armv7-M and Armv8-M; interrupts off on Armv6-M

documented_interrupts.text: alloc from an ISR with timeout 0; free from an ISR

configurations.name: C_Allocator fb_allocator (C)
configurations.lock: ALLOC_LOCK_NONE, the library's default without threads

documented_interrupts.text: may be called from an interrupt with an interrupt-masking lock option; without threads the default is no lock (as built here)

configurations.name: MemoryPool Fixed (C++)
configurations.lock: none on the boards; std::mutex on the host

documented_interrupts.text: without threads not thread safe (#warning); no lock on the boards

configurations.name: heapless pool, BoxPool (Rust)
configurations.lock: lock-free: LL/SC on the boards, a tagged CAS on the host; not on Cortex-M0+

documented_interrupts.text: only on ARM cores with LDREX, CLREX and STREX; lock-free
